title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 29
paragraphs: The Parians reconciled the factions in the following way. Their best men came to Miletus, and seeing the Milesians in a disastrously ruined state, they said they wished to go over the country. While doing this and passing through the whole territory of Miletus, whenever in the desolation of the land they saw any field that was well cultivated, they wrote down the name of its owner. Then when they had gone through the whole land and found only a few such men, as soon as they returned to the city they called a general assembly and appointed to manage the state those whose fields they had found well cultivated—for they said they thought these men would care for public affairs as they had cared for their own; and the rest of the Milesians, who had before been divided by factions, they commanded to obey these men.
